topic: All-in cost of a South Orange County, CA presence (Aliso Viejo / Laguna Niguel / Laguna Hills / Mission Viejo / Laguna Beach) for Integra Dental Design: footprints A (150-400 sf office), B (600-1,200 sf flex finishing/QC satellite), C (1,200-2,000 sf production lab), plus California tax, licensing, labor, insurance, utility and travel costs. Desk research, accessed 2026-10-12.
summary:
Bottom line: small space in South Orange County is findable and not expensive at the unit level; the California compliance and labor stack, plus the fact that a leased satellite by itself drags the whole WA LLC into California tax jurisdiction, is where the cost sits. Against Integra's reconciled ~$11,700/month of collections, a staffed Footprint B runs roughly $6,500-7,000/month all-in (about 55-60% of current collections) and Footprint C roughly $10,000-11,000/month before materials. Footprint A is roughly $2,200-2,500/month including one monthly trip. Note: WebSearch budget was exhausted at the start of this task; all discovery ran through Exa search/fetch. LoopNet detail pages were readable via Exa search snippets but not by direct fetch.

FACTS (primary sources, accessed 2026-10-12). Space: live listings include 400-460 sf second-floor offices at 27992/28052 Camino Capistrano, Laguna Niguel at $700/month Modified Gross (updated Jan 20, 2026) and a 1,600 sf flex unit in the same park at $2,800/month MG; 1,200 sf flex at 23372 Madero, Mission Viejo at $1.75/sf/mo (utilities and property expenses excluded); 1,768 sf flex at Saddleback Business Park, 27071 Cabot Rd, Laguna Hills at $2.00/sf/mo with a fixed $0.35-0.36 CAM and 100-200A three-phase power; 1,920-1,960 sf at 23322 Madero at $1.75; 2,800 sf NNN at 23561 Ridge Route at $1.70/sf/mo (updated Sep 26, 2026); 809 sf full-service office at 27141 Aliso Creek Rd at $2.45/sf/mo; 207-402 sf suites at 85 Argonaut, Aliso Viejo at $41.76-57.96/sf/yr. Market context: Kidder Mathews 3Q 2026 puts South County average direct asking industrial rent at $1.71 NNN (Laguna Hills/Aliso Viejo $1.67 at 2.8% vacancy; Mission Viejo $1.77 at 0.7% vacancy; Laguna Niguel/Laguna Beach has only 291,371 sf of industrial inventory in total), so sub-2,000 sf units near Aliso Viejo are scarce rather than cheap. Executive-suite benchmark: Regus 15 Enterprise, Aliso Viejo private office from $519/month on a 1-month minimum. Taxes: CDTFA Regulation 1506(e) makes dental labs retailers taxed on the entire charge to dentists; Regulation 1591(b)(5) explicitly lists crowns, bridges, dentures, inlays as not medicines (taxable), while 1591(b)(2) lists dental implant systems including bone screws and abutments as exempt medicines when sold to a dentist for treatment, so separately stated abutment charges can be exempt. The combined rate in Aliso Viejo, Laguna Beach, Laguna Hills, Laguna Niguel and Mission Viejo is 7.75% (effective July 1, 2026). A CA office is physical presence requiring CDTFA registration for all CA sales; without it the remote-seller threshold is $500,000 of CA sales (RTC 6203, AB 147). FTB: Form LLC-5 registration fee is $70; the $800 annual LLC tax applies to any LLC registered or doing business in CA (first-year waiver ended for years starting on/after Jan 1, 2024); the gross-receipts LLC fee starts at $900 only above $250,000 of CA income. FTB "doing business" thresholds for 2025 are $757,070 sales, $75,707 property, $75,707 payroll. Payroll: 2026 CA UI new-employer rate 3.4% on $7,000, ETT 0.1% on $7,000, SDI 1.3% employee-paid with no wage cap; minimum wage $16.90; EDD projects 2026 FUTA at 2.1% ($147/employee) because California is a credit-reduction state. Workers' comp class 4692 (Dental Laboratories) advisory pure premium is $1.48 per $100 effective Sep 1, 2026 (secondary source citing WCIRB; CDI approved an average benchmark of $1.65). Wages: EDD/OEWS for the Anaheim-Santa Ana-Irvine MD (2026 Q1) show dental lab technicians at a $21.89 median, $18.02 25th percentile, $29.17 75th percentile; Orange County employment is about 1,230 with flat 10-year projections. Current Irvine postings: $18-22/hour entry (Glidewell, Ultimate Staffing, Simply Biotech, Aug-Oct 2026); Keating Dental Lab $40-65k for experienced techs. Licensing: Aliso Viejo, Laguna Niguel, Laguna Hills and Mission Viejo have no business license tax; each requires a certificate of occupancy/business registration (Laguna Hills COUO $250.10). Laguna Beach taxes gross receipts ($60 base + 0.00044-0.00088 per dollar, $1,650 cap) plus a $414 use-and-occupancy fee. California has no dental-lab registration statute; labs operate under the BPC 1626(e) exemption requiring a dentist's signed written authorization, and 17 CCR 10446 exempts labs from device-manufacturer licensing. Travel: Alaska flies 6-7 daily nonstops SEA-SNA; Saver one-ways were $89-149 for November and $279-293 for mid-October departures on 2026-10-12; IRS mileage is 76 cents (Jul-Dec 2026).

ESTIMATES (labeled): build-out for a furnace/compressor/ventilation satellite $8,000-60,000 (base $25,000) using OC contractor benchmarks of $12-35/sf for TI electrical and $8,000-30,000 for panel capacity; NNN add-ons $0.35-0.65/sf/mo from three disclosed South OC pass-throughs; security deposit 1-3 months (no statutory cap under Civil Code 1950.7; a new foreign LLC should expect the high end or a guaranty); electricity 23-31 cents/kWh (EIA CA commercial averages) giving $200-500/month for B and $400-1,000 for C; liability insurance $1,500-3,500/yr bundled for a small lab per a specialty broker, full package $3,000-7,000; employer payroll load 11-15% of wages for a part-time tech including WC.

UNKNOWNS: whether a dental lab is permitted by right in the specific business-park zoning (Aliso Viejo instructs tenants to verify before signing); Laguna Niguel and Mission Viejo C of O fees and Aliso Viejo's business-registration invoice amount; carrier WC minimum premium; sales-tax treatment of screw-retained titanium bars; actual insurance quotes; CalSavers and OCFA hazardous-materials triggers; landlord appetite for a 1-year or month-to-month term for a WA entity. A separate consequence worth flagging: Oregon HB 2594 (effective July 1, 2026) requires out-of-state labs serving Oregon dentists to register with Oregon's HLO and provide material disclosures, which touches the Harmony Dental (Eugene) account regardless of the California decision.

findings.claim: Dental laboratories are retailers in California; sales tax applies to the lab's entire charge to a dentist
findings.detail: CDTFA Regulation 1506(e): 'Dental laboratories are the retailers of the plates, inlays and other products which they manufacture for dentists or other consumers. Tax applies to their entire charges for such products regardless of whether a separate charge or billing is made for materials and manufacturing services.' Dentists are consumers. Accessed 2026-10-12.
findings.source_date: Business Taxes Law Guide Revision 2025 (undated page)

findings.claim: Crowns, bridges, dentures and inlays are explicitly not 'medicines'; dental implant systems including abutments are exempt medicines when sold to a dentist for treatment
findings.detail: Regulation 1591(b)(5): prosthetic devices that do not qualify as medicines include 'dental prosthetic devices and materials such as dentures, removable or fixed bridges, crowns, caps, inlays, artificial teeth' - taxable like any TPP. Regulation 1591(b)(2): permanently implanted articles that qualify as medicines include 'dental implant systems including dental bone screws and abutments'; exempt when sold to a licensed dentist for treatment of a human being under 1591(d)(4). Implication: separately state abutment vs crown on implant-crown invoices; treatment of screw-retained Ti bars not addressed. Accessed 2026-10-12.
findings.source_date: Business Taxes Law Guide Revision 2026 (undated page)
findings.value: Crown taxable; abutment exempt if separately stated and sold to dentist

findings.claim: Combined sales/use tax rate is 7.75% in Aliso Viejo, Laguna Beach, Laguna Hills, Laguna Niguel and Mission Viejo
findings.detail: CDTFA city/county rate table lists each of the five cities at 7.750% (Orange County). Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: A California office or representatives create sales-tax nexus for the whole company; without physical presence the remote-seller threshold is $500,000 of CA sales
findings.detail: CDTFA Wayfair/AB 147 guide: retailers with physical presence (e.g., 'maintaining inventory or office locations in California', representatives taking orders or making deliveries) must register; remote sellers must register and collect when total CA deliveries exceed $500,000 in the preceding or current calendar year (RTC 6203 as amended by AB 147, Stats. 2019 ch. 5). Integra's current CA sales (one SoCal dentist account) are far below the threshold, so no collection duty exists today; CA dentists owe use tax as consumers. Accessed 2026-10-12.
findings.value: $500,000 remote threshold; $0 threshold with physical presence

findings.claim: Foreign LLC registration (Form LLC-5) filing fee is $70
findings.detail: SOS Form LLC-5 states 'Filing Fee - $70.00', optional certified copy $5.00, $15 special handling for in-person submissions; must attach a current Certificate of Good Standing from Washington. Form notes registered LLCs may owe the $800 minimum tax. Statement of Information (LLC-12) is $20, due within 90 days then biennially (standard SOS fee; not re-fetched). Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: Every LLC registered or doing business in California owes the $800 annual tax; the gross-receipts LLC fee begins at $250,000 of California income
findings.detail: FTB: $800 annual tax due by the 15th day of the 4th month, 'even if you are not conducting business'; first-year exemption applied only to tax years beginning 2021-2023. LLC fee: $900 at $250,000-$499,999 CA income; $2,500 at $500k-$999,999; $6,000 at $1M-$4.99M; $11,790 at $5M+. Integra's ~$140k/yr total revenue would currently be below the $250k fee threshold even if all CA-sourced. Form 568 must be filed. Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: A leased CA satellite with a part-time employee will likely make the WA LLC 'doing business' in California on the property or payroll test even before registration
findings.detail: FTB 2025 thresholds: CA sales > $757,070, CA real and tangible property > $75,707, or CA payroll > $75,707 (or 25% of totals). FTB apportionment rules value rented property at 8x annual net rent (standard Schedule R convention; not re-fetched), so a $2,800/month lease (= $268,800 of property) alone exceeds $75,707; engaging in any transaction for financial gain in CA also qualifies. Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: 2026 California employer payroll taxes: UI 3.4% new-employer rate on $7,000; ETT 0.1% on $7,000; SDI 1.3% employee-paid with no wage cap
findings.detail: EDD: new employers assigned 3.4% UI for two to three years; 2026 schedule F+ range 1.5%-6.2%; taxable wage limit $7,000. ETT 0.1% on $7,000. SDI withholding 1.3% for 2026, all wages subject (SB 951). Accessed 2026-10-12.
findings.value: UI $238 + ETT $7 per employee per year

findings.claim: California employers face an elevated FUTA rate: 1.8% final for 2025 and a projected 2.1% for 2026 ($147 per employee) because of the state's outstanding federal UI loan
findings.detail: EDD DE 202 (Rev. 15, 1-26) footnote: projected 2026 FUTA rate for California employers reflects the outstanding federal UI loan; final credit reduction published after Nov 10, 2026. Federal Register notice (Jan 12, 2026) finalized the 2025 California credit reduction at 1.2% (total 1.8%, $126/employee). DOL's potential 2026 figure is 5.3% (1.5% + 3.8% BCR add-on) if the add-on waiver is not granted; waivers have been granted every year so far. Accessed 2026-10-12.
findings.value: $126 (2025 actual) to $147 (2026 projected) per employee; worst case $413

findings.claim: Aliso Viejo has no business license program but requires a Business Registration (Form PS-250) with floor plan and Planning zoning clearance before operating; TI and signage need separate building permits
findings.detail: City page: 'Although the City of Aliso Viejo does not have a Business License program, businesses are required to obtain approval from the Community Development Department prior to the start of business operations.' Tenants are told to contact Planning (949-425-2525) before signing a lease to confirm the use is permitted; some uses need an AUP/CUP. Registration is invoiced after submittal; fee amount not published on the pages retrieved. Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: Laguna Beach levies a gross-receipts business tax ($60 base plus 0.00044-0.00088 per dollar, $1,650 cap) plus a $414 Use and Occupancy fee, $20 application fee and $4 CASp fee
findings.detail: Municipal Code Ch. 5.08 (rates effective Jan 1, 1996: Group 1 $60 + .00044 x gross receipts; Group 2 $60 + .00088; max $1,650). HdL/RevDS new-application form: Use and Occupancy Fee $414 for brick-and-mortar locations, Home Occupation $120, CA CASp $4, Application $20; 10%/month penalty. Business tax certificate also required for out-of-city businesses conducting business in Laguna Beach (e.g., deliveries to Laguna Beach dentists). Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: California does not register or license dental laboratories; labs operate under the Dental Practice Act exemption requiring a dentist's signed written authorization with each order, and are exempt from state device-manufacturer licensing
findings.detail: BPC 1626(e) exempts construction/repair of crowns, bridges, dentures and other prosthetic appliances when casts/impressions are made by a licensed dentist, 'but a written authorization signed by a licensed dentist shall accompany the order for the work'; labs may not hold themselves out to the public as providing dental services. 17 CCR 10446 exempts dental laboratories manufacturing dental prostheses from H&S Code 26685 licensing. The restorative-materials fact-sheet duty (BPC 1648.10-1648.20) falls on dentists, not labs. NADL materials list California among the 40+ states without lab registration; BPC 1683.1 concerns telehealth, not labs. Accessed 2026-10-12.
findings.value: No registration fee; written authorization required

findings.claim: Oregon HB 2594 (effective July 1, 2026) requires dental labs located outside Oregon that do business with Oregon dentists to register with the Oregon Health Licensing Office and provide material-content disclosures
findings.detail: NADL announcement: registration applies 'to dental laboratories that are located in Oregon and to facilities that are located outside of Oregon but do business with Oregon dentists'; registered lab must employ a dentist, CDT, or technician with acceptable CE (5-year grace period for CDT). Relevant to Integra's Harmony Dental (Eugene, OR) account independent of the California decision. Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: California commercial security deposits have no statutory cap; Civil Code 1950.7 only governs holding, permitted deductions and return timing (30 days after possession)
findings.detail: CIV 1950.7 (amended Stats. 2003 ch. 89): landlord holds deposit for tenant; may apply to rent defaults, damage, cleaning; return within 30 days (two weeks for the portion above one month's rent when claim is rent-only); bad-faith retention damages up to $200 plus actuals. Market norm for small tenants is one to two months; a newly registered out-of-state LLC with no CA operating history should expect two to three months or a personal guaranty (estimate). Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: Small dental lab liability insurance: bundled professional + general + product liability at $1M/$3M typically $1,500-3,500/yr; standalone GL $600-1,200/yr; full small-lab package $3,000-7,000/yr
findings.detail: Homewood Insurance (dental lab program page, undated): small-to-mid lab with clean record $1,500-3,500/yr for bundled professional/GL/product; GL alone $600-1,200; 30-70% surcharges for digital workflows or remake claims; property/BPP written standalone or in a BOP at replacement cost. GeneralLiabilityInsure.com: $1M/$2M GL for small labs $67-99/month. Joyce Insurance (NY context): small lab basic package $3,000-7,000/yr; cyber $1,000-3,000. Sebrite Agency runs a national dental lab program since 1986 (no prices). No California-specific quote obtained (desk research only). Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: California commercial electricity averaged 30.56 cents/kWh (EIA, data through July 2026) and 23.13 cents/kWh in January 2026; SCE small-business customers (<20 kW) take service on TOU-GS-1 with 4-9 p.m. summer on-peak pricing
findings.detail: EIA Electric Power Monthly Table 5.6.A as reported by Voltcheckr/electricityrateperkwh (July 2026: CA commercial 30.56c vs US 14.53c) and powerbillfacts (Jan 2026: 23.13c). SCE TOU-GS-1 fact sheet (July 2025): customer charge plus TOU energy charges; Option E has no demand charges. EIA-861-derived SCE commercial average ~23.09c. Accessed 2026-10-12.
